terms.gloss: a system, a method; an order worked out by reason
evidence: Cic. Fam. 1.8.4: commūtāta tōta ratiō est
Cic. Off. 3.20: Stōicōrum ratiō disciplīnaque (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: order, system; a theory or doctrine; a method. A judicial system, ratiō jūdiciālis (Traupman 195).

terms.gloss: a system of teaching or doctrine; a way of doing things
a whole made of parts; a technical system
terms.comment: Greek σύστημα; in Latin only late (Martianus Capella). Traupman uses it for a stereo system and a computer’s operating system.

phrases.latin: commūtāta tōta ratiō est senātūs, jūdiciōrum, reī tōtīus pūblicae
phrases.english: the whole system has changed: the senate, the courts, the entire state
take care not to scorn someone else’s system rashly

sources: Lewis & Short: ratio · Lewis & Short: disciplina · Lewis & Short: ordo · Lewis & Short: systema
